criteria.claim: Closed workflow, phase and work-state enums with v2 session and interface contracts
Nil versus empty AllowedTools survives JSON and nested scope/work arguments cannot alias
Batch approval RFC 8785 bytes and SHA-256 match shared Go/browser vectors
Every historical class is deterministic and no single field grants executable authority
Both workflows use one durable executor with fail-closed checkpoints and receipt accounting
Browser edits bind revision and hash, cancellation is run-bound, v1 controls are read-only
A sync -> async -> sync batch and a multi-call iterative response resume after reconstructing every service and execute each eligible item exactly once without dropping the tail
Replayed terminal events and replayed consumption do not duplicate observations or transcript entries, open extra observers, or advance the cursor twice
Cancellation during model work, dispatch, observation and restart prevents successors while retaining submitted-effect accounting; stale targets cannot stop a newer run
A receipt-less dispatching item becomes uncertain, is never replayed, blocks successors and resolves only through verified request-event evidence

Hooks tighten but never loosen, changed approved input never executes, batch approval stays mandatory, action approval binds one work item, and nil/empty AllowedTools hold across workflows and restart
Observation keeps one scoped backfill-plus-live subscription per receipt; EOSE never completes it; CLOSED/AUTH blocks (projection only) and reissues; provenance is validated
v2 session projections have strictly increasing created_at per session, including same-second transitions and across restarts
Recovery is one path: v1 history converts once through the pure classifier; accounting-only conversions never dispatch or reason; ambiguous history parks

Only the unified executor dispatches assistant work: the orchestrator's direct batch dispatch and submittedPlans, AgentLoop Execute/ExecuteWithHooks dispatch, the runtime session persister/metadata writes and observeDownstreamResult are removed; subagent child calls are gated and synchronous-only

Workflow selection is explicit request > persisted session > assistant.default_workflow (falling back to the deprecated agentic flag); the flag never gates construction; a second prompt against an awaiting, executing, waiting, cancelling-with-accounting or blocked run returns run_in_progress

Joined real-service flow: batch proposal edited (reorder/delete/argument change) and approved with the revision-bound v2 hash executes exactly the approved sequence once across a full restart with no model request on continuation; approval cannot bypass a changed permission policy or the persisted command scope

Unversioned v1 approvals follow Decision 6: unedited plan-hash approval only for the matching migrated awaiting draft, edited ModifiedPlan refused with approval_contract_upgrade_required without state change, action-ID only for the unique migrated pending action, plan-hash cancel only for the migrated current batch run, v2-native runs require v2 contracts

Production wiring passes the engine and store to startup recovery, which resumes in-flight runs instead of parking them; unknown session IDs are proven new by a scoped EOSE lookup; v1-only history is read-only; a session-scope cancel on a finished run stays enforced after restart

Internal tools (subagents, skills) keep their service-owned registration outside the batch catalog and pass the common scope/schema/policy/hook gate as executor work; the iterative proposer returns whole responses and owns a restart-proof model-iteration cap; nil/empty/out-of-scope AllowedTools hold with the real proposer
